p.t: In short

Change the look in the **Customizer** first. Touch the code only when the Customizer truly cannot do the change.
Click **Save** after every change, then check the live page.
Show only real things. Remove fake or empty social links and unused sections, because suppliers will click them.
Finish the homepage in about **60 minutes** when your images are ready, following the set order.

Keep **one slide** in your homepage slideshow. Add more later if you need them.
Link a page or button only when the destination page already exists.

Check the store on a **phone** before you save.
Remove fake text and placeholder phone numbers before launch.
**Save** after every change, or the edit is lost when you leave the editor.
**Check the mobile view** before you save, because a page can look fine on a computer and broken on a phone.

**Add links only to pages that already exist**, or visitors hit dead ends.
Keep **social media off** until real accounts exist.
**Hide** a section instead of deleting it, so you can bring it back later.
The checkout (the payment page) is mostly locked. A full redesign needs Shopify Plus, a paid plan of about **2,500 USD per month**.
Make the checkout banner **1500 × 300 px**, the size most sources give.
Trust badges (security logos, guarantee, payment icons) helped one store's conversion rate (share of visitors who buy) go from **0.29% to 2.15%** in one day.
**Check your plan** before you promise a custom checkout.
Theme editor access and basic rules
The **Theme Customizer** is Shopify's built-in visual editor.
It changes a theme's look without touching code (code is the written instructions that make a website work).
It adjusts the website font, color scheme, layout and store content from a side panel on the customized themes page.
Use the Customizer's built-in settings for **everyday look changes** first.
Go into the theme's HTML/CSS (HTML is the page structure code, CSS is the style code) only for structural changes the Customizer cannot make.
Avoid editing theme code unless a change truly cannot be made in the Customizer. Opening the code editor by accident means you are in the wrong place for ordinary design work.
Admin path (the back office menu inside Shopify, called the admin): **Online Store > Themes > Customize**. The Source A Manhattan theme must be installed to use this path.

Steps to open the theme customization pages:
1. Log in to the Shopify account.
2. Click **Online Store** in the Shopify admin.

3. Click **Themes**.
4. Find the installed theme named Source A Manhattan.
5. If it is the **currently published** theme (published means live for visitors), click the **Customize** button.
6. If you are upgrading from another theme and Manhattan is not yet published, find it in the list of unpublished themes further down the page and click **Customize**.
7. The side menu that opens lists the elements you can edit. Changes made there alter what visitors see on the store.
Before opening the theme customization pages, the basic store should already have its **menus** (the lists of links), some **collections** (groups of products, like shelves)
Theme editor access and basic rules (continued)
and a **demo product** (a sample item used for testing). The Customizer then turns that bare structure into the finished look.
To open the homepage editor, go to **Online Store > Themes**, confirm the active theme is the one you are building, and click **Customize**.
Check that the page dropdown (the menu at the top of the editor) says **Homepage** before you change anything.
In the sidebar, hovering over a section highlights it on the page. Clicking an element in the preview opens its settings. Each section can be hidden with the **eye icon** or removed with **delete**.
Sections can be reordered by dragging the **six-dot handle** (the grip you drag up or down).
The left sidebar shows the homepage layout from top to bottom. Hovering a section name highlights it on the live preview. Clicking an element on the preview jumps to that section in the sidebar.

Click **Save** after every change in the theme editor. Then reload the live product page to confirm the change appears. The preview does not always show the final result, for example end dates or hidden blocks.
**Theme settings** apply to the whole store, including fonts, buttons and header. **Section settings** only affect the one section they belong to.
Each section's color scheme dropdown uses the named color schemes defined in Theme settings > Colors (a color scheme is a saved set of colors).
One color change therefore updates every section that uses that scheme.
Collection pickers in the collection list and featured collection sections only show collections that already exist.
Create and fill the collections under **Products > Collections** first, then add them to the homepage.
Order of work and time budget
Budget **60 minutes** to complete the full homepage customization when image assets (ready image files) are already created.

The work is mainly placing those assets.
Work through the homepage in this order:
1. Upload all images to **Files**.

2. Set **logo** and **favicon** (the small icon shown in the browser tab).
3. Set **colors** and **typography** (the fonts and text sizes).
4. Set **layout** and **buttons**.
5. Set **header**, **sticky header** (a menu bar that stays at the top while scrolling) and **menu colors**.

6. Configure **slideshow** (a rotating set of large images at the top), **collection list**, **featured collection**, **pre-footer** (the strip above the footer at the bottom of the page) and **email signup**.

7. Hide unused sections.
After each step, **save** and check the preview on **desktop and mobile**.
The same work can be seen as four blocks:

Homepage and general customizations.
Menu customizations (header and footer menus).
Collection page customizations (layout and visuals).
Product page customizations (layout and settings).

Theme customization turns a Shopify store from its default basic template (gray, white and black) into a branded store. You do this by adding image assets and adjusting layout and settings inside the theme editor.
Advanced web design changes are **optional final tweaks**. They suit a store that already performs well and needs extra gains. They are not needed to get first results.
Shopify's native editor is moving toward more **page-builder** flexibility (a page builder lets you move blocks around without code). For example, you can move elements without code.
This cuts the developer work needed for simple layout changes.
Full Manhattan homepage procedure (initial setup)
The complete homepage walkthrough, in order, as taught for the Manhattan theme:
1. Upload all image assets. Go to **Shopify Admin > Content > Files**, click **Upload files**, select all Canva assets (Canva is a design tool) at once, and confirm the upload completes.
2. Open the theme customizer. Go to **Shopify Admin > Online Store > Themes**, select the Manhattan theme, click **Customize**, and confirm **Homepage** is selected in the top dropdown.
3. Hide the announcement bar (the thin strip at the very top of the store). Hover over **Announcement bar** in the sidebar and click the **eye icon**.
4. Add the logo. Go to **Theme settings** (gear icon) > **Logo**, select the uploaded logo file, and keep the desktop logo width around **200**.
5. Add the favicon. Go to **Theme settings > Favicon image** and select the small logo variation file.
6. Set global colors. Go to **Theme settings > Colors**, use your brand hex codes (a hex code is a short code that names one exact color), and keep the palette to **2-4 colors**:

Accent 1 (primary brand color).
Accent 2 (secondary brand color).
Text (black).
Background (white).

Background 2 (light gray).
Then click **Save**.

7. Set typography. Go to **Theme settings > Typography**. Set the **Heading** font to a display font (a bold, eye-catching font). Set the **Body** font to a readable clean font, for example Montserrat.
Optionally increase the **Font size scale** to **110%**. Then click **Save**.
8. Adjust layout. Go to **Theme settings > Layout**. If you want, increase **page width** to **1600** (measured in pixels, the dots on a screen). Then click **Save**.
9. Remove social media defaults. Go to **Theme settings > Social media**. Remove the default URLs (web addresses) if you have no active accounts yet, then save.
10. Enable the sticky header. Go to **Header > Sticky header**, turn on **Always on**, and save. Preview the page to confirm the header stays visible on scroll.
11. Set the header menu. Leave **Menu** as **Main menu**. Set **Desktop menu type** to **Mega menu** (a large drop-down that shows many links at once).
12. Add header contact details. Go to **Header > Contact details**. Add service hours (optional) and an email, for example support@yourdomain.com. Replace the email with a phone number later on.
13. Customize header colors. Go to **Header > Navigation menu color**.
Full Manhattan homepage procedure (initial setup) (continued)
Update the **Background color**, **Link colors**, **Dropdown background**, **Dropdown link colors** and **Border colors**, using only your brand palette. Then save.

14. Configure the slideshow:
Use **1 slide** only.
Delete blank slides.
Set **Slide height** to **Adapt to first image**.

Keep full width.
Add the hero image asset (the big main picture).
Add a **Heading**, for example a primary collection focus.

Add a **Subheading** that states a benefit.
Add a **Button label**, for example Shop Now.
Link the button to the relevant collection.

Position the content, for example bottom right.
Align the text, for example right.
Adjust button colors if needed.
Save.

15. Set up the collection list (a row of group tiles):
Change the heading to **Shop Our Featured Collections**.
Set **Image ratio** to **Adapt to image**.

Set **Columns** to **3**.
Optionally add a text overlay (words placed on top of the picture).
Add **6 collections**, for example Best Sellers, Staff Picks, Top Rated, New Arrivals, On Sale Now and Under $1000.

Go to **Shopify Admin > Products > Collections**, open each one, add an **Image**, and save.
Refresh the theme customizer.

16. Hide the rich text section (a block of free-form text). It is not needed for supplier approval.
17. Configure the featured collection (one group of products shown in a row):

Change the heading, for example What's Trending in Surfing.
Select a collection, for example Best Sellers.
Set **Products to show** to **4**.

Set **Columns** to **4**.
Toggle **Vendor** (the brand name), **Ratings**, **Secondary image** and **Quick View** (a pop-up preview of a product) on or off as you prefer.

Choose a color scheme.
Save.
18. Configure the email signup. Change the headline to branded text, for example Join Shaka Nation. Leave the default form. Choose a matching color scheme. Save.
19. Configure the pre-footer. Add **4 columns**, each with an icon and a short benefit headline. Example headlines: Free Shipping $100+, Surfer Owned & Operated, Fast & Secure Checkout, Easy Returns.

Add links only if the pages exist. Set the background to white if it looks cleaner. Save.
20. Hide the blog posts section. It is not needed for supplier approval.
21. Refresh the homepage and scroll through it. Confirm the store looks legitimate, has no dead links (links that lead nowhere), uses consistent branding and has clean, supplier-ready sections.
Global settings: logo, favicon, colors, typography and layout
Set the **desktop logo width** to **200 pixels** in Theme settings > Logo. The default is usually acceptable.
Increase the page layout width to **1600 pixels** in Theme settings > Layout for a wider, more spacious look.
To make the page narrower instead, go to **Online Store > Themes > Customize**, click the gear icon for Theme settings, and open **Layout**. Type a value into **Page width** or drag the slider.
Spacing and padding (the empty space around content) are controlled in the same section.
Note on width: the **1600** setting makes the page wider. The **Page width** field in the same Layout section is the way to make it narrower. This contrasts with 2024 advice.
Keep the global palette to **2-4 colors**. Use brand hex codes and the roles listed under Colors.
Keep color changes in **Theme settings > Colors**, because every section's color scheme draws from there.
Open the theme customizer and click the gear icon labelled **Theme settings** to reach the extra features.
p.h: Theme settings: search, pop-ups and custom CSS

p.t:
Work through the settings in the order they appear in the panel.
In the Manhattan theme settings panel, the sections appear in this order:
1. Search behavior.

2. Email pop-up settings.
3. Exit pop-up (a box that appears when a visitor is about to leave).
4. Cross-sell (suggesting related products).

5. Social proof pop-up (a box showing that others bought recently).
6. The Source A tracking option.
7. Custom CSS.
Review them from top to bottom. Click **save** after changing the tracking option.

Search behavior: keep **search suggestions** turned on, and turn on showing the **product price** within those suggestions. This controls what happens when visitors click the magnifying glass and search the store.
Custom CSS field: paste code here to change how the store looks when the theme editor has no normal option for it. Use it only for appearance changes that cannot be made in the normal theme settings.
Social media links
Remove the default social media URLs from **Theme settings > Social media** if you have no active accounts.
Suppliers must not click social icons that lead to Shopify's default pages.
Turn **off** the footer social media icons if you do not have real social profiles yet. Never send suppliers to a store with dead or placeholder links (placeholder means fake filler text).
Footer social icons in the Manhattan theme only appear for social channels that have a **full URL** entered in the theme customizer. Check each link, including the full https:// address, then save.

**Footer > Show social media** can stay on even with no links, because the icons only show real links. Add links later through the gear icon, in the social media fields, and make sure the show-link option is on.
If no social pages exist yet, delete the empty links.
Do not lead the header navigation with social media links such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, YouTube or Pinterest.

Shoppers who came to buy should first see **shop pages, collections and product categories**.
Conflict on footer social icons, by situation:

**No real social profiles yet**: Off (footer social media icons off)
**Turning on before accounts exist**: Do not do it; visitors reach pages that do not exist

**Profiles exist, full URLs entered**: On; icons show only for entered links
**Show-social toggle on with no links**: Allowed; icons simply do not show
Source A's 2025 Manhattan footer reference value is **off** until social accounts exist.
Header
In Shopify Admin, go to **Online Store > Themes > Customize**. Select **Header** from the left sidebar. Make sure your **Menu** setting references **Main menu**.
Confirm that your **Desktop menu type** is set to **Mega menu**, the standard theme default.
**Header > Sticky header** with the **Always on** option keeps the menu bar visible while visitors scroll. A related option shrinks the logo on scroll. This helps when the logo file is large.
Sticky header set to **Always on** keeps the menu visible while scrolling. Customers can always reach the menu without scrolling back to the top.
**Header > Desktop logo position** offers **Top left**, **Top center**, **Middle left** and **Middle center**. Top left is the common default for most stores.
**Header > Show separator line** adds a thin line under the header. It is on by default. Turn it off for a cleaner header.
**Header mobile layout** lets you move the logo on phones, for example to center or left. This is separate from the desktop position. Always save, then open the store on a phone to check the result.

The header in the Source D theme editor has these settings:
A **Menu type** setting (for example Sticky header).
A **Separator line** option.

An **Enable top border** option, with a color set to **Use Theme Colors**.
A **Middle left** position set to **Main Menu**.
Scroll-up behavior is controlled by the **On scroll up** option.
Header contact details, as in the default setup: add service hours (optional), add an email, and replace it with a phone number later on.

Customize header colors: go to **Header > Navigation menu color**. Update the **Background color**, **Link colors**, **Dropdown background**, **Dropdown link colors** and **Border colors**, using only your brand palette.
Then save.

A large header logo that pushes content down wastes vertical space. Use the empty header space for a short message that helps the buyer, for example free personalized note cards included with every order.
A header that only says "welcome to our store" is generic and wastes the top of the page.
Replace it with a **call to action** (a short message that tells the buyer what to do, like "Shop Now") or a **scarcity message** (a message that says stock is limited).
Header (continued)
Fast themes often ship with demo homepages and headers not built for sales. Examples include social media icons first in the header and oversized hero slideshows.
Right after installing a theme, reconfigure the header, homepage and collection layout for shopping instead of keeping the demo structure.
Older method (2020): to place the logo in the same row as the menu, people edited code. They opened the theme editor and the **code editor**, then copied and pasted the required code.
If you were not comfortable with code, you could **hire a Shopify developer on Upwork** (Upwork is a site where you hire freelancers).
Native option versus the older code method: the 2020 approach used header code.
The current **Desktop logo position** setting in the Header section offers Top left, Top center, Middle left and Middle center **without code**.
By default, hide the announcement bar by hovering over it in the sidebar and clicking the **eye icon**.
If the theme has a built-in announcement bar section, build the bar there by entering the text and the code in the theme's customization settings.
Use a separate **app** (an add-on tool you install from Shopify's app store) only when the theme does not offer this, or when you prefer another solution.

An announcement bar at the top of the store can show a **sitewide promotion** (an offer shown on every page), for example a **10 percent** discount. Competitor stores use it to push a current offer on every page.
Use the **Quick Announcement Bar** app only if you want different promotions shown on different supplier pages. Otherwise, the theme's built-in announcement bar is enough. Older advice (2021).
The **coupon code bar** (the bar showing a discount code) at the top of the store is edited in Shopify admin under **Store**, then **Store settings**.
If it still appears after you change the theme, check the store settings first. Older advice (2020).

In the header bar editor, you can increase the **text font size**, but you cannot set the bar height directly. If no adjustment is possible at all, check the app or theme for a problem. Older advice (2019).

Conflict on announcement bar, by purpose:
Hide it while building, if there is no promotion yet.
Use the built-in bar for a **single sitewide message**.
Use an app only for **different messages per page**.
Homepage structure and what to show
Homepage structure, in order:
1. Show **one hero value proposition** (the one big promise at the top) that states the core benefit for the target audience.

2. Link straight to **best sellers** (the most-bought products) and the product range.
3. Give a short explanation of what the product does and how it differs from alternatives.
4. Offer **bundles** (several products sold together) and **subscriptions** (repeat delivery on a schedule) to lift **average order value** (the average amount one buyer spends per order).
5. Add **testimonials** (customer quotes) and **social proof** (signs that other people trust the store).
6. Add **authority logos** from recognised media in the niche (logos of respected outlets in your market), placed higher up the page.
Arrange the homepage sections in the same order as the theme's demo store. Copying the working layout cuts setup time. Older advice (2020).
The home page should not replace the product page. If the home page is the only page a visitor sees, the shop is set up wrong and **conversion** (a visitor who buys) suffers.
In a single-product store, the product should be the main page.

Group the homepage around **one clear store theme**. A homepage that mixes unrelated categories, such as gag gifts, surf, apparel and novelties with no gift theme, looks random and makes navigation hard.

A store must make sense **within seconds** for visitors arriving from a Facebook ad, a Google ad or any other source. Navigation, logo and copy should together show who the store is for and what it sells.
For a single-category fashion store, organize the homepage into collections by **dress type**. Give each collection a hero image showing a person wearing the items.
This gives visitors a clear path into the collections and makes the store look like one focused range.
A homepage layout example uses square collection images in rows of **three**, followed by a row of three more. A best-sellers collection sits next to the main product collections.
This layout needs **six square** homepage images.
Homepage collection tiles can be arranged in rows of three. For example, six tiles in two rows. Place the most popular collections, such as a best sellers collection, where customers see them first.
Remove unused default Shopify sections from the homepage, such as an empty video section or a promotions box with no content. Leftover empty sections add clutter and signal an unfinished store.
Homepage structure and what to show (continued)
Competitor layouts will not map one to one onto a different theme. Rebuild the same **section type** (the kind of block, such as a proof block or FAQ block) with your own theme's settings.
Keep the purpose of each section, such as proof, FAQ (frequently asked questions) or transformation (before and after), even when the design changes.
Video carousels (rotating video blocks) and slider sections are built into almost every Shopify theme, especially Atlas and Shrine.
When you recreate a competitor layout, use the sections your theme already offers instead of custom development (building new code from scratch).

Quick navigation section above the main banner, as taught in the Source E course:
1. Display **5-6** visual category shortcuts.

2. Style them to resemble **Instagram story cards**, a visual pattern shoppers recognize.
3. Include current sales and new product promotions.
4. Position the section **above the fold** (the part of the page visible without scrolling) for immediate visibility.
**Recently viewed products** can be enabled in the theme editor under the Recently viewed products section (Settings > Enable recently viewed products).
This setting applies to both collection pages and product pages. It helps returning customers, but shows nothing until a visitor has viewed products. Older advice (2021-22, Source B's theme).
Steps to set up the homepage slideshow (the rotating picture block at the top of your home page, also called the **hero**):

1. Open the **Slideshow** section in the editor (the screen where you change how your store looks).
2. **Delete** extra blank slides and keep one.
3. Click the first slide, **select an image**, then click Done.
4. Enter the **heading** (the large main line of text), the subheading (the smaller line under it), the button label (the words on the button) and the button link (the page the button opens).

5. Then **set the content position** for desktop and mobile. Desktop means a computer screen. Mobile means a phone.
Full default slideshow steps (the complete setup list):

1. Use **1 slide** only.
2. **Delete** blank slides.
3. Go to Slideshow > Slide height. **Select Adapt to first image**, so the slide height follows the first picture.

4. **Keep full width**, so the slideshow fills the whole screen width.
5. **Add the hero image asset**, which means a picture file already uploaded to your store.
Slideshow (hero) (continued)

6. Add a **Heading** (example: primary collection focus).
7. Add a **Subheading** (benefit-oriented). This means a short line that says what the customer gains.

8. Add a **Button label** (example: Shop Now).
9. **Link the button** to the relevant collection. A collection is a group of products shown together on one page.

10. **Position the content** (example: bottom right).
11. **Align the text** (example: right).
12. Adjust the **button colors** if needed.

13. **Save.**
A new Shopify slideshow comes with **three blank slides**. Shopify is the online store software you use.
For a supplier demo store (a sample store that shows suppliers how your store will look), **one slide is enough**.

You can add more slides later with **Add a slide**, for new suppliers or seasonal sales.
Slideshow settings:
**Layout:** Full width or Grid layout.

**Slide height:** set to adapt to the first image, or to small, medium or large.
**Pagination** (the small markers that show which slide you are on): dots or numbers.

**Auto rotate** (slides change by themselves): set to every **3, 5 or 9 seconds**.
**Animation style:** controls how one slide changes to the next.
The **accessibility field** holds a short description of the slideshow.
A screen reader (a program that reads the page out loud for people who cannot see well) reads this description to those visitors.

Something like "a slideshow about your brand" is **enough**.
Slide content settings:
Heading.
Subheading.

Button label.
Button link.
Desktop content position.
Desktop alignment.

**Show container on desktop.** A container is the box that holds the text.
Button color.
Button text color.

Mobile alignment.
In the example, the content sits **bottom right**, aligned right. The button label is Shop, and it links to a collection.
**Button text** must contrast with the button color. Contrast means the two colors are clearly different, one light and one dark.

If you change the button to a dark brand color (your store's main color), **set Button text color to white**.
Otherwise the label becomes unreadable on the slide.
Slideshow (hero) (continued)

After changes, **preview** the slideshow on a phone. A preview is a test view before visitors see the store.
If the text covers the image, **adjust the mobile alignment**.

**Save only after** the mobile view looks right.
Slideshow images that look cut off are usually the **wrong size** for their space.
**Crop** (cut off the edges) or **resize** (change the size of) the image to the required dimensions before uploading. Dimensions are the width and height of the picture.

This is older advice from 2019.
A hero image is **one image** shown on both mobile and desktop.
So you **cannot upload separate versions** for each screen.

To enlarge it on mobile, **make the image taller in pixels**. Pixels are the tiny dots that make up a picture.
Making it taller also enlarges it on desktop.
Hero slideshows should follow the **conversion layout** above, not the demo structure. A conversion layout is a page design that helps visitors take the wanted action, such as buying or signing up.
Oversized (too big) hero slideshows are a **demo default** to replace. A demo default is a sample setting that came with the theme.
Homepage logo list: in the **theme customizer** (the editor for your store's look), choose the homepage.

A theme is the design template your store uses.
Click **Add section**, then select **Logo list**.

Enter a **heading**, such as Brands loved by our customers or Featured brands.
**Upload supplier logos.** A logo is a brand's picture mark.

**Link each logo** to the matching collection.
Use the **three-dot menu** and **Duplicate** to add more logos.
Section spacing has two parts.

**Padding** adds space inside a section, around its content.
**Margin** adds space between sections.
In the header example, the **bottom margin is 0**.

In the same example, the top and bottom padding are **20 px each**. px means pixels.
**Adjust padding** to change space inside a section.

**Adjust margin** to change space between sections.
For a logo list that scrolls sideways (horizontally), use this AI prompt (a written request you type into an AI tool) **unchanged**:
I'm looking to add a logo list for the brands I sell for on my homepage that scrolls horizontally. Please create the code.

I would need to create a new section in Shopify, so please send step-by-step installation instructions and show exactly where to put the code. My store link is [STORE URL]. Brand logo files: [LOGO FILES].
Collection list

Collection list section settings:
**Heading** (example: Shop our featured collections).

**Heading size** (small in the example).
**Image ratio:** set to **adapt to image**. Image ratio is the shape of the picture, width to height.

**Collection description:** off by default.
**Number of columns on desktop:** 3 in the example.

**Text overlay**, with position bottom left. A text overlay is text placed on top of the picture.
**Overlay color.**

Set the collection list grid to **3 columns** when showing several featured collections on the homepage. Featured collections are collections you want to highlight. A grid is boxes arranged in rows and columns.
**Enable view all** lets mobile visitors swipe through extra collections. Mobile means a phone.
**Turn it on** if you add more collections than fit on the screen.
With **3 columns** on desktop, **six collections** fill two rows on the homepage. Six is the count used in the example.
Add more collections **only if** they fit the layout and will be filled with products.
Example names for 6 collections: Best Sellers, Staff Picks, Top Rated, New Arrivals, On Sale Now, Under $1000.

These names show suppliers and customers that the store is organized and actively managed.
To add collections to the list:

1. Click **Collection** in the collection list section.
2. Click **Select collection** and pick a collection you created earlier.

3. Click **Add collection** to add the next row.
4. Repeat until the list is complete, then click **Save**.
Default setup steps:

1. **Change the heading** to Shop Our Featured Collections.
2. Set **Image ratio** to Adapt to image.
3. Set **Columns** to 3.

4. Add a text overlay if you want one. It is optional.
5. **Add 6 collections.**

6. Go to **Shopify Admin > Products > Collections**. Shopify Admin is the back office where you manage your store.
7. Open each collection.

8. **Add an image** to each collection.
9. **Save.**
10. **Refresh** the theme customizer, which means reload it.
Featured collection

Featured collection section settings:
**Heading** (example: What's trending in surfing).

**Collection** (example: Best sellers).
**Number of products:** 4.
**Number of columns:** 4.

So **four products** show in **one row**.
Show **4 products in 4 columns** in the featured collection section on the homepage. This gives a balanced look.
A featured collection section with **real products** on the homepage makes your store look like an active business with products to sell.

This matters for both supplier approval and customer trust.
A product card is the box that shows one product. Its options:

Show or hide a **secondary image** (a second picture of the product).
Show or hide the **vendor** (the brand or seller name).

Show or hide the **product rating** (the star score from buyers).
Set the **sale badge** position. A sale badge is a small label, such as "Sale."

Set the **sale badge color scheme** (its set of colors).
**Quick view** is a pop-up that opens a product on the same page.
When Quick view is **on**, the product opens in place, with an **add to cart** button. Add to cart puts an item in the shopping basket.
When Quick view is **off**, the visitor goes to the product page.
Use **5 to 10 products** for the best sellers, top rated and staff picks sections on the homepage.
Best sellers are the products that sell most. Top rated means the highest reviews. Staff picks are products your team chooses.

This is 2023 advice. It differs from the 4-product setup above.
Apply the 5 to 10 rule to those sections only.
Image banner

An image banner is a wide picture with text on top.
Image Banner section on the homepage:

1. **Hide** the section if you don't have content ready.
2. If using it, **select an image**.
3. **Add a heading** (example: Buyer's Guide).

4. **Add description text** and **button labels**.
5. **Add button links only if** destination pages exist. A destination page is the page a link opens.

6. Optionally **enable ambient movement** for a subtle motion effect.
7. **Save.**

Use this section for **buyer's guides** (guides that help a buyer choose) or featured content.
Image banner section settings:
The **image**.

**Banner height:** adapt to first image.
**Desktop position:** middle center.

Pre-footer trust columns
The pre-footer is a section of columns just above the footer. The footer is the bottom area of every page.

The pre-footer section holds several columns.
Each column has an image, a header (a short title), a description and an optional link.

Set the color scheme to **Background 1 (white)** for a clean look on a white page.
Steps to configure the pre-footer:
1. **Add 4 columns.**
2. Add an **icon** (a small symbol picture) and a short **benefit headline** to each column. A benefit headline is a short title about what the buyer gets.

3. Example headlines: Free Shipping $100+, Surfer Owned & Operated, Fast & Secure Checkout, Easy Returns.
4. **Add links only if** pages exist.

5. Set the **background to white** if it looks cleaner.
6. **Save.**
Only **link pre-footer columns to pages that already exist**.
Leave a column **unlinked** until its page is created.
Broken links lead nowhere. Placeholder links are fake links that stand in for real ones. Both look unprofessional when a supplier clicks through.
**Link policy pages**, such as shipping and returns, in the pre-footer once they exist. Policy pages explain the store's rules.

Until then, a **temporary link** to an existing page is acceptable.
An example temporary page is terms of service, the rules for using the store.
Replace the temporary link **later**.

Trust column pattern: a **short benefit headline**, followed by **one reassuring sentence**. The sentence explains how the benefit is delivered.
The headline is **2 to 4 words**.

The description **names the concrete promise**.
Example: Free returns for 30 days, Refunds go back to the original payment method within 5 business days.

Example: Secure payment, Checkout is encrypted and card details are never stored on our site.
Business days are working days, usually Monday to Friday.

You can use **fewer** than seven.

Examples: free shipping, a price match guarantee (a promise to match a lower competitor price), a women-owned or veteran-owned business (owned by a former soldier), a secure checkout,

or 24/7 customer service (help at every hour).

Footer: placement, structure and rules
The footer is a global section. A global section is one that appears the same on every page.

The footer appears on **every page** of the Shopify store, including the home page.
You edit it in the theme editor, under the Footer section.
From there you configure:

**Menu blocks** (boxes of links). A block is one box of content inside a section.
**Payment icons** (logos of accepted payment methods).

**Language and currency selectors** (buttons to switch language or money).
**Small footer text.**
**Rich text blocks** (text areas you can format).

This is older advice from 2021-22, from Source B's theme.
Footer setup in Shopify, using the Manhattan theme (a store design template):

1. Open **Shopify admin**, go to **Online Store > Themes**, then click **Customize**.
2. **Confirm** the theme is Manhattan.
3. Stay on the homepage view, **scroll to the bottom**, and **click the footer section**.
4. Set the **main footer settings**: color scheme, localization (language and currency settings), payment icons, and social media (icons that link to your social accounts).

5. Set the **top and bottom padding**.
6. Edit the **first column** as Contact us.

7. Edit the **second column** with the store name and its linked menu.
8. Edit the **third column** as Quick Links, and link its menu.

9. Edit the **fourth column** as the newsletter signup.
10. Click **Save**, open the live store, refresh it, and check the footer.
11. **Adjust the logo size** if needed, save again, then exit the admin.
Footer setup in the theme editor, in this order (an alternative sequence with the same goal):
1. Open the **footer section** in the left navigation. The footer has four blocks: Contact us, store name, Quick links and newsletter signup.

2. **Block 1 (Contact us):** open it in the left navigation, so its settings appear in the right sidebar. Set the heading to **Contact us**. Set the text to **Reach out**, or a more playful line that fits your store.
3. **Block 1:** enter the support email address in the email field, for example support@yourstore.com.
4. **Block 1: delete the placeholder phone number.** A phone number is not needed when contacting suppliers.
5. **Footer image:** click the image box. Choose the **same logo** used as the main logo in the header. Set the **image width** to **50%**.
Footer: placement, structure and rules (continued)
6. **Click save**, go back to the store, and refresh the preview to check the result.
7. **Footer styling:** choose the color scheme, set the heading size to **small**, set top padding to **40** and bottom padding to **40**.

8. **Footer styling:** keep payment icons **on**, and switch social media icons **off**.
9. **Block 2:** rename the block to your store name, and choose the footer menu as its menu.
10. **Block 3:** title the block **Quick links**, and choose the quick links menu as its menu.
11. **Block 4 (newsletter signup):** replace the default newsletter text with your own wording, then click save.

12. **Refresh** the store and check that all four blocks show the right content.

**Footer image width**: 50%

**Heading size**: small
**Top padding**: 40
**Bottom padding**: 40
**Payment icons**: on

**Social media icons**: off until social accounts exist
**Block 1 heading**: Contact us
**Block 1 text**: Reach out, or a playful alternative

**Block 2**: store name, menu: footer menu
**Block 3**: Quick links, menu: quick links menu

Contact block.
Store-name menu block (Footer menu).

Quick links menu block.
Newsletter signup block.

To add a new block, you must **delete one** first.

This is older advice from 2021-22.

Once the footer is set up on the home page, it **does not need further changes** until launch.
The next step is to edit the collection and product page layouts.

This is older advice from 2021-22.

Demo content includes placeholder phone numbers (fake stand-in numbers), sample addresses, default text and demo menus (sample menus).

This content stays visible on the live store if you leave it.
Check **every footer block** on the home page against the real business details before going live.

This is older advice from 2021-22.

**Create the footer menu and the quick links menu** before assigning them to blocks 2 and 3.

2. **Create the Quick Links menu**: About Us, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Contact Us.

4. **Upload the store logo.**

Option 2: click the block directly in the store preview.

Footer first column (Contact us section):

Set the heading to **Contact us**.
Enter a short text such as Reach out.
Add a business email address.
Optionally add a phone number.

Upload the store logo as the footer image.

Newsletter signup block (the box where visitors type their email to get your news) in the footer. Procedure:
1. **Click** the Newsletter signup block in the footer.
2. Change the **headline** (the big title of the box) to something more engaging. Examples: Join [Brand Name], Get Updates, Join Shaka Nation.
3. Keep it **simple** and brand-appropriate (fitting your brand's style).
4. **Save** and refresh the storefront preview. Refresh means reload the page. The storefront is the public view of your store, as visitors see it.

Footer fourth column (newsletter signup): keep the **default** layout.
Change only the headline to a short, catchy line.
Write the headline yourself, in the same style as the example pattern described below.
Newsletter headline pattern: a short, playful, **lowercase** line (no capital letters) that gives a reason to join. It sounds like a community, not a sales pitch.

Formula (the fill-in pattern): [action verb] + [group or identity] + [small benefit or hook].
A hook is a short reason that grabs attention.

New examples in this pattern: join the surf crew and get the first drops; be first in line for new arrivals.

1. **Click** Footer in Theme Customizer (the editor where you change how the store looks), not a block, to access global footer settings.

2. Set **Heading size** to Small. Heading size is how big the title text is.
3. Set **Padding top** to 40. Padding is the empty space around the content.

6. Turn **Social media icons** OFF.

Pick the one that matches the brand colors chosen earlier.

treats padding as a finer-control option.

Footer localization (country or region selector, which shows the store for different places): leave it **off** unless the store sells in several countries or regions.
Turn it on only in that case.
Language selector: in the Manhattan theme footer settings (Manhattan is one of Shopify's design templates, called a theme), the Language selector toggle (on/off switch) sits next to the Localization

(country/region) toggle.

Turning it on brings them back.

Check every footer block against the real business details.

Hiding vs deleting sections
A section is one block on a page, such as a banner. The theme editor (Shopify's page editor) lets you change sections.

Use **hide** instead of delete when customizing sections in the theme editor while building.
Hide removes the section from view without deleting it.

Hiding lets you undo or reconfigure the section later.
Delete removes it **permanently**.
Each section can be hidden with the eye icon or removed with delete.
Hide the rich text section (a text block with formatting), since it is not needed for supplier approval. A supplier is the company that makes or ships your products.

Hide the image banner (a wide picture across the page) until content exists.
Or add links before it goes live.
Hide blog posts (articles on the site) until content exists.
Unused default Shopify sections should be **removed** from the homepage (the front page of the store).
Examples of unused default sections: an empty video section or a promotions box with no content.
Only add hyperlinks (clickable links) or button links to sections if the destination pages **already exist**.
Broken links (links that lead nowhere) damage the appearance of a legitimate, professionally managed store.
Include a **search bar** and continue shopping button on your store.

Customers who cannot easily search or navigate to other products abandon the site (leave without buying) immediately.
Older advice (2020).
On stores with many products, place a **large search bar** in the header of every page. The header is the top area of each page.

The search bar should be easy to find.
It should be large enough to use comfortably on desktop (computers) and mobile (phones).

Older advice (2021-22).
Moving the search bar in the theme requires editing theme code (the programming behind the design).

**Copy and paste the original code** before editing, so the change can be reversed.
Preferably have a developer (a person who writes code) do it.
Older advice (2022).
Customizing the cart page (where buyers see the items they chose) natively in Shopify. Natively means with the built-in tools, no code.

3. Select **Cart** from the drop-down menu (a list that opens when you click).
4. Edit elements such as the logo, reviews or contact info.

Checkout (the payment page) customization options available **without Shopify Plus** (a higher-level Shopify plan).
These options include changing the checkout background, the logo and adding a banner at the top of the checkout.
A banner with a phone number or support text can be effective in some industries, such as weight-loss products.

It appears in the checkout header.

Check that the layout still looks clean.

Refresh the homepage and scroll through it.
Confirm the store looks legitimate.

Avoid editing theme code unless a change truly cannot be made in the Customizer.
Shopify sanitizes raw HTML (HTML is the basic web code; sanitizing removes parts that could be unsafe).
When the theme editor cannot produce a custom page, a Shopify specialist on Upwork (a site where you hire freelancers) can build the fix.
They build it for a **one-time fee** (you pay once).
Third-party landing page builders (outside tools for making single sales pages) are usually **monthly subscriptions** (you pay every month).

Some landing page builders cost more than Shopify itself.

Add the floating widget (a small tool that stays in place on the page) to the Shopify homepage. Procedure:

1. In the Shopify admin, go to **Online Store > Themes** and click **Customize**.
2. Open the homepage and click **Add section**.
3. Search for **Custom Liquid** or HTML and add the section. Liquid is Shopify's code language. HTML is the basic web code. The name depends on the theme.
4. Set Section padding for Top padding and Bottom padding to **0px** (px means pixels, a unit of size).

5. Make the section background invisible (use the section settings in the theme editor).
6. Paste the widget code into the Custom Liquid field.

7. Click **Save**, then refresh the storefront to see the floating widget.

If you cannot find the Custom Liquid section, search for **HTML** in the section list instead.
Theme editor workflow: opening and saving the editor
Open the theme editor through **Online Store > Themes > Customize** on the active theme (the theme that is live now).

Homepage content is built from sections that can be **added, removed and reordered** in the editor.
Store changes are kept only after you click **Save**.

Unsaved edits are lost when you leave the editor.
Save after every change or set of changes.
Save before moving to another settings area.
The preview updates in real time (instantly as you change things), but only **Save** keeps the edit.
Before you edit, check that the dropdown at the top reads **Homepage**.
Theme settings and section edits for the homepage must be made on the Homepage template (the version of the page that the homepage uses).
The customizer shows the homepage preview on the **left** and the editing sidebar (side panel) on the **right**.

Hovering over a section (moving the mouse over it) highlights it on the page.
Clicking the section opens its settings.
Always switch the editor to **mobile preview** before saving.

Check the header and footer separately in each view.

2. Choose Mobile, Desktop or Full screen from the dropdown.

3. Select the same logo image for mobile if needed, then adjust the **mobile logo size** separately.

Theme editor workflow: adding, removing and reordering sections
Shopify themes build the homepage from sections.
Each section adds a specific block such as a slideshow, featured collection (a group of products shown together) or grid (products in rows and columns).

The default demo sections are placeholders, and most should be **removed** for a new store.
To add a homepage section:
1. Click **Add section**.
2. Choose the section type, for example Featured product.

3. Select the new section, add the content, and choose the product or details it should show. New sections are added at the **bottom** of the page first.
To remove a homepage section:

1. Click into the section.
2. Click the **three dots** (the menu icon with three dots) at the top of the section panel.
3. Choose **Remove section**.

To change section order, click and hold the six-dot handle (the grip you hold to move something) of a section.
Then **drag** it to a new position.
In the Manhattan theme, the Add section option is available on every template (the page-type layouts).

In the Manhattan theme, it offers the same section types as the homepage.
Each one can be previewed before it is added.

This lets a page carry more than rich text.
