Products: set Sale badge style (the label showing a discount) to **Save $10**, Option style to Selectable boxes, Display stock levels (showing how many items are left) to **Hidden**,

Quick shop button (a button to buy without opening the product page) to **Disabled**, Add to cart button to Enable on desktop only, Show dynamic checkout button on (a fast pay button such as Apple Pay),
and enable color swatches (small color circles to pick a variant).

6. Social media: leave until launch, then add Facebook, Pinterest, email address and Instagram.
7. Favicon: upload the favicon PNG (a type of image file).

8. Cart: no change needed.
9. Custom styles and scripts (hidden code added to the store) and Advanced: leave **untouched**.
10. Performance (speed settings): keep the preset defaults.
11. Checkout: upload the logo as a custom image, set logo size to Medium, change the button color to match the site buttons and the accent color to the main brand color, and leave error messages red.
12. Click **Save** before leaving the editor or moving to another settings area.
Header
Header settings include **Logo position, Menu type, Header borders** (lines around the header), and a Top Border Style option.
Top Border Style can use the theme color or a global section gradient (a color that fades from one shade to another).

Desktop and mobile font sizes are set separately in the theme settings.
Check both views.
Sticky header (a header that stays at the top while you scroll) set to **always on** keeps the logo, menu and contact information visible while the visitor scrolls.

An option also shrinks the logo on scroll.
Desktop logo position: **top left** is the default.
Other options are top center, middle left and middle center, which rearranges the header elements.
Separator line: a thin line under the header, **on** by default. It can be turned off.
Menu font size **14** and font weight 500 are the typical values. Font weight means how thick the letters look.

Change the size only if the chosen font looks too small or too large.
Contact details: set opening hours for customer service.

Add a phone number and email address once they exist.
An email alone is acceptable at the supplier stage.

Mobile layout: logo position can be set separately for phones, for example center or left.
Preview on a phone after saving.
Menu field: the default is **Main menu**.
To use another navigation menu (a list of links in the header), click Change, then Change menu, and select a menu created earlier in Shopify.

The header should contain the brand logo, the main menu links, the search function (the search box) and the cart.
Shopify adds search and cart to the header by default.

For a new store you only need to **select the menu** to show.
Customer login or account links are optional.

Make the logo **smaller** and place it on the left side of the navigation bar (the row of links).
Visitors care more about the products than the logo, so a large logo wastes space.
Header layout and mobile search (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice)
Set the header layout in theme settings under Layout to **Traditional** instead of Minimal.

Only the Traditional header shows a search bar.
Changing the layout means header section settings are no longer applied.

Check the header after switching.
In the Traditional header layout, the search bar stays visible on mobile in this theme, which many themes do not do.

Check on the mobile preview that the search bar and logo still fit the header.
Enable the sticky header in the static header settings (the header's own settings group).

Select the logo image in the header so it displays.
Adjust the logo height so it is readable without being too large or too small.

Enable the **utility bar** (a thin bar above the header) in theme settings.
Add a top bar menu to it.
Use a background matching the footer, white link color and yellow link hover color. A hover color is the color a link turns when the mouse is over it.
A secondary menu (a second list of links) can be placed on the right side.
Edit the **announcement bar** (a thin strip at the very top of the site) under Online Store > Themes > Customize by

clicking the announcement bar section.
Change the message text there.
Add an icon such as a shipping symbol if needed.

The header can carry a scrolling promo bar (a strip for offers) for savings or shipping lines.
The header can also carry a top row with Track Your Order and Support links.

It can have a country and currency selector. Currency is the money used for prices.
Set the currency selector so buyers see prices in the **currency they will pay in**.

Hide the announcement bar until it is needed.
Older advice (2021-2022) states that in a Shopify theme the announcement bar is fixed and cannot be removed.

The Manhattan setup above **hides** it instead.
Use hiding rather than deleting if you are unsure.
Slideshow and hero banner: Hero banner principles
A hero banner is the big picture and text at the top of the homepage.
A homepage banner should show the customer's **outcome** (the result they want) or passion, so a visitor immediately sees they are in the right place.

Its main job is to state what the business does for the customer.
A temporary promotion is a secondary use.
A hero banner needs four elements: a title, a subheader (smaller text under the title), social proof, and a **call to action**.

Social proof is a sign that others trust you, such as review counts or numbers of items saved.
A call to action is the button or line that tells the visitor what to do next.
A missing call to action is one of the most serious gaps.
Homepage banner pattern: > [Store name] introducing [top-rated or number one rated] [product] for [customer type] in [country], paired with a benefit-driven image,
followed by a short section on why the product helps and what the store stands for. It works because the visitor instantly sees the brand, the product and a clear benefit.
Example one: Lumora introducing the top rated travel pillow for frequent flyers in Germany. Example two: Brinelo introducing the best rated desk mat for home offices in the UK.
Homepage structure for a niche store (a shop for one specific interest) begins with a banner that matches the feeling of the exact customer.

Most traffic (visitors) arrives via ads directly to product pages.
So keep the page clean and branded.
Slideshow layout: **full width** (used in the example) or grid.

Slide height set to **Adapt to first image** so the image is sized correctly. Slide height is how tall the picture area is.
Size options small, medium and large exist.

Pagination (the dots or numbers that show which slide you are on) can be dots or numbers.
Auto rotate (slides change by themselves) can change slides every **3, 5 or 9 seconds**.
Set mobile content to show below images.
Give the slideshow a short accessibility description (a text that describes the images for people who use screen readers, programs that read the page aloud).
Slideshow settings (Manhattan and Superstore themes) (continued)

Slide content: heading and subheading go on top of the image.
The button label is **Shop**.

The button link (where the button sends the visitor) points to a collection.
Desktop content position **bottom right** and alignment right were used in the example.
Slideshow content settings let you set the button colour and the button text colour separately.
A container background (a colored box behind the text) can be shown behind the text on desktop.
Choose a button text colour that **contrasts** (is clearly different in shade) with the button colour, so the label stays readable.
Slideshow section margins (space outside the section) add space above or below the whole section.

Use them to adjust the gap between the slideshow and the sections around it.
Keep **one slide** for the demo store.
Delete the blank default slides.
Add more with Add slide later for new suppliers or sales events (times with special offers).
Buttons in image banners and slideshows look faded or nearly transparent while they have no link.
Their full colour shows only after a real destination, such as a collection, is set in the **button link** field.
Slideshow settings in the Shopify theme editor include Enable slideshow, Autoplay slideshow, Autoplay slide duration and Slideshow height.

The image field recommends **1800 x 1000 px** (width by height in pixels).
Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice.

A slide's BUTTON 1 has the fields Label, Button, Link and Style.
Style is set to **Primary** (the main button look).
Clearing the Label field (the words on the button) **hides the button**.

The same panel holds the Heading, Subheading, Text color and Text alignment (Left) fields.
Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice.
Slideshow settings (Manhattan and Superstore themes) (continued)
Older advice (2021-2022) states that homepage sliders should **not be used**.
JavaScript (code that makes pages move and change, which can slow a page) slows the page.

The cited figure says about **96%** of customers never see the second slide.
A single hero image at the top of the homepage is enough.
Older advice (2021-2022) for the early-stage store: the slideshow is used as a single static hero image, which is fixed in the section list.

Conflict (two sources disagree): the older no-slider advice and the single-static-hero advice both point toward one image.
The Manhattan setup keeps a slideshow with one slide.

A **one-slide slideshow** matches both.
A multi-slide rotation is what the older advice warns against.

Four small images side by side on desktop should **stack vertically** (one above the other) on mobile.
On a phone they become too small to read.

They can also trigger Search Console accessibility errors. Search Console is Google's tool that reports site problems, and accessibility errors are problems that make the site hard to use for some people.
Keep the stacking instead of forcing a side-by-side layout on mobile.
Collection list settings (Manhattan theme): heading "Shop our featured collections" in a small heading size,
p.h: Collection lists and featured collections: Collection list

p.t: image ratio set to Adapt to image so mixed image sizes fit, and desktop columns set to 3.

Text overlay on, placed bottom left, overlay colour teal from the brand palette, text white. Enable view all lets mobile visitors swipe through extra collections.
Adding collections:

1. Click Collection and choose a collection with Select.
2. Click Add collection to create a new row for more items.

3. Repeat until all collections are set, then Save. The example used six collections in rows of three.
Superstore theme setup:
1. Add the Collection list section and set the heading to Our Featured Collections.
Collection lists and featured collections: Collection list (continued)

2. Set Desktop section spacing to 100 px (the maximum) and Mobile section spacing to 60 px.
3. Keep four collections per row and delete any extra blocks.
4. For each block, click Change, select a collection that has products, and click Select so its product image loads automatically.
5. If a collection has no products, upload a custom image of a similar product type. Otherwise it shows a blank image.

6. The collection title fills in automatically. Overwrite it with a custom title if needed.
7. Click Save.
A collection without products shows a blank image in the featured collections section.
Use a custom image as a temporary placeholder and replace it with real supplier products when the store goes live. (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice.)
A simple homepage can feature the newest collection and a section with trending products. These two sections give a first-time visitor a clear starting point.
Featured collection (Manhattan theme): change the heading to a short phrase such as What's trending, select a collection such as Bestsellers,
and show 4 products in 4 columns. Product card options include secondary image, vendor and rating.
Quick view shows a button that opens product details in place with an add-to-cart option. If turned off, the button leads straight to the product page.
Sale badge: the product card settings include a sale badge position, a sale badge colour and an editable badge text.
The badge defaults to a dark gray background and can be switched to a theme accent colour such as the pink accent.
Keep featured collections linked only to collections that exist and contain products.
The Featured collection section in the Superstore theme started with a beige background set by the theme.
A white background is acceptable, and a light contrasting background can break up a long white homepage. Either can be changed in section settings.
Image banners and image-with-text sections
Image banner (Manhattan theme): set the image as background, banner height Adapt to first image,
desktop position middle center, container turned off so text sits directly on the image,
and buttons linked to a collection once it exists.
Image banner > Image behavior: None keeps the image still. Ambient movement makes the image move very slowly, which draws the eye to the banner.
Highlights banner (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice): desktop section spacing starts at 36 px and mobile at 20 px, with banner text centered.
The tested build raised desktop spacing to 60 px.
Create the destination pages first, such as Shipping, Contact us, Returns and Price match guarantee, before building Highlights banner blocks. Each block link must point to an existing store page.
Shrine theme Image with text settings: Heading, Text, Link button, Image or Video, Media height (Adapt to media), Color schemes (Content color scheme and Section color),
Desktop layout (Full page width) and Remove section. Use autoplay mp4 video that is muted and looping instead of GIFs or animated WEBPs.

Icon Bar: each icon uses the Check available icons search, so search for a soft word like pillow first. If no icon matches, scroll to the custom icon option and paste the icon code to replace the icon.
Shrine sections such as Image with text have a Display section ID field. Paste that ID into any button link so the button scrolls to the section, or use it to merge two sections.
Logo list for shipping carriers as proof: go to Online store, open Customize for the theme, click Add section, search for Logo list and add it, then upload the logos.
You can delete the text to make it smaller, change the size, background and padding, and drag it to any position.
Logo lists can show well-known customers. This is useful for business-to-business products.
Pre-footer trust columns
Each pre-footer column has an image, a header, an optional description and a link.
The example used a gray background, changed to background 1 (white) for a cleaner look.
Pre-footer trust column pattern: each column pairs an icon image with a short benefit header that tells the visitor why the store is reliable, such as shipping threshold, origin or checkout security.
Example 1: Free shipping over 75 dollars. Example 2: Secure payment at checkout.
Security cues such as trust badges belong on the cart and checkout pages as well. They reassure shoppers at the point where they decide to pay.
Homepage section for a single-niche store includes trust signals and a risk-free message.
Footer structure in the theme editor: Brand description, Text column (contact information), Useful links column,
and Legal links column with Privacy Policy, Shipping policy, Refund policy, Terms of service and Contact information. Upload a footer logo from the library and link each policy page.
Add footer text by opening the footer section, clicking Add block, and choosing Text. Write the About Us text with the brand mission, email address and business address, then click Save.
Add a footer logo by clicking Add block in the footer section and choosing the Image block. Upload the logo, increase its size so it is clearly visible, and click Save.
The footer should contain a customer care section with the links visitors look for, plus an about section.
Visitors who land on a product page see the navigation first and scroll to the footer next, so it must support them.

The footer should contain a get-in-touch section, support hours, support email addresses, a live chat link and links to social media pages. Footer links to unrelated pages make the store look untrustworthy.
Footer editing is done in the same customizer sidebar and is a separate step. Cookie consent is a pop-up set in the same sidebar and can be switched on or off.
Do not link any section or footer item to a page that does not exist yet. Suppliers clicking dead links see a broken store, so leave link fields empty until the target page is created.
Repeat the Highlights banner near the bottom of the homepage with a different background color than the footer, so two identical colors do not sit next to each other.
Use a second color from the brand palette. (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice.)
Pages and blog (Manhattan theme): Editing a page template
Open the theme editor, click the template dropdown at the top,
switch from home page to Pages, and select the default page (the About Us page) to

edit it. A separate Contact page template also exists.
In each page's settings in the Shopify admin, adjust padding, margin and width (full width or narrower, centered).
Each page type has its own template in the theme editor.
To give a page different sections than the default page or the contact page, create an additional page template instead of changing the existing ones.
Add a logo list with a heading such as "Brands we've worked with" by clicking Add section and adding logos one by one.
Make sure blog posts are published and visible, because hidden posts do not show in the listing.

Blog listing settings: choose Grid or Collage layout. Collage shows the newest post at the top, while Grid shows posts evenly. Featured images are recommended to be shown, and image height can be set.
Show or hide date and author, and set card or standard layout in theme settings.
Card or standard layout and the background colour under post titles are set in the theme settings and are separate from the grid or collage choice.
Blog posts template: adjust padding, margin, page width, featured image size (Adapt to image keeps the uploaded size), title, date and author visibility, and the share link.
With Adapt to image, the featured image becomes full size based on the uploaded image size. Keep the page width unchanged so it matches the rest of the site.
Keep the blog post page width at the theme default. A narrower width makes the post text noticeably less wide on large monitors and stops it from matching the rest of the site.
Blog post pages show a share link by default that lets readers copy the post URL. Keeping it visible is recommended. Hiding it is possible but not advised.
Add an Email signup section to the blog posts template: enter a heading, click Save, optionally change the accent color, then Save again.
Hide Rich text and Blog posts sections in the first version of a store with no content yet. Enable them later when content exists.
Cart page: Manhattan theme cart setup
To edit the cart, open the Theme Customizer, click the page dropdown at the top and scroll to the cart entry.
The checkout entry is in the same dropdown but cannot be edited; only the cart can be changed.
Customers reach the cart either by clicking the cart icon after adding a product or by being sent straight to the cart, depending on the add-to-cart behaviour in the product page settings.
The cart page must therefore work as a standalone step before checkout.
The default cart page keeps the header, the mega menu built earlier and the footer. These global elements can stay without changes.
Items section: shows the products the customer has added. Its padding and margin controls move the content up or down. No changes are needed in a default setup.
Subtotal section: shows the subtotal, the checkout button and the order special instructions field. Its padding and margin can be adjusted the same way as the Items section.
Cart note: in the cart's theme settings it can be enabled or disabled. When disabled, the order special instructions text disappears from the cart page after saving and reloading the store.
Keep the cart note enabled. Customers sometimes write notes there, and these are saved to the Shopify order information. Disabling it removes a channel for useful customer requests.
Do not modify or hide the checkout button, because customers with items in the cart must always be able to proceed to checkout.
Additional blocks such as a countdown timer or a coupon are added inside the cart template through the add block option.
Each block is placed by moving it in the customizer, and its colours and text are set in its own settings.
Adding extra content such as rich text sections to the cart page is usually unnecessary and can distract buyers from checkout. Add sections only when there is a clear reason.

Cart page setup order:
1. Open the Theme Customizer and select cart in the page dropdown.

2. Check the Items and Subtotal sections and adjust padding or margin only if spacing needs fixing.
3. Open Theme settings and keep the cart note enabled.

4. Leave the checkout button unchanged.
5. Add any optional blocks such as the urgency timer or the coupon only when they are needed.
6. Click save and reload the storefront to check the result.
Cart page content and checks
Check the cart page by adding a product from the storefront and opening View cart, because the cart page is empty until a product is added.
Text on the cart page can be changed through the theme's default content settings.
Optimise the cart page, which many stores neglect, because it is where shoppers start to doubt the purchase.
Add USP messaging, shipping details and upsells there, presented the same way as on the product page.
Reconfirm unusual shipping requirements on the cart page as well as on the product page. Upsells that some shoppers missed on the product page can also be shown on the cart page.
Cart in the Superstore theme needed no change in the early-stage settings order.
Layout choice at creation is Single Column or Double Column.
A Double Column cart gives cart line items a dedicated area, which suits carts with long item lists such as parts and accessories. The layout can be switched later without starting over.
Advanced settings pull typography from the Shopify theme's typography settings. The title heading level can be changed, for example from H1 to H2, to get the wanted font without custom CSS.
The cart title can also be hidden entirely, for example to place a store logo with custom CSS.
The country field in Smart Cart v2 suggests matching countries as you type, so merchants do not need to know the two-letter ISO code. In v1 this code had to be typed in directly.

The order notes component collects a gift message or special instructions. These notes appear in the order attribution section on the right side at the top of the Shopify order, not under the line items.
The cart subtotal has singular and plural label fields, and the item count can be inserted with a variable. Keep the subtotal label simple, since heavy changes are rarely needed.
The Express checkout block in the Smart Cart editor is only a placeholder and does not appear as text on the live store.
The buttons that show depend on the accelerated checkout methods connected in the Shopify admin and the express checkout preferences set there.
They can display as separate buttons in a row instead of one combined block.
Homepage structure and order of work: Principles
The homepage is the first page visitors see on the root domain and the hub of the site.
It should introduce the business, state what is good about it, give reasons to buy, and introduce the products sold.
It connects to all other pages through the main menu, the bottom navigation and the search bar.
In high-ticket dropshipping the reseller sells the same products as other sites, so the homepage must sell the business as well as the products. Customers compare where to buy as well as what to buy.
At launch the competition is on identical products; a brand's own products come later.
A weak store design holds back sales even when ads perform. Improve the store before running ads, with better images and a clear layout.
Homepage imagery must match the store's product type. Show people using the products and link to the category collections of that product type.
A homepage that mixes lifestyle photos unrelated to the products confuses visitors and makes the store look incoherent.
Shopify core components are the announcement bar, header, footer and the main page types (home, product, collection, cart, blog and checkout). Set up these components before adding more content.

The home page can stay simple with two or three sections: a banner related to the current product, the product itself, and a benefits section with badges such as priority shipping and money-back guarantee.
Homepage structures by store type

Niche store (procedure, as the lesson describes it):
1. A banner that matches the feeling of the exact customer.

2. An About Us or mission section telling the brand story.
3. One or two sections for the main product.

4. A collection of products. Keep it clean and branded, since most traffic arrives via ads directly to product pages.
Single-niche store, in this order:

1. Headline with the offer and a big benefit, such as a percentage discount.
2. Striking product visuals.
3. Review badge that links to the reviews section.

4. One customer testimonial.
5. More product images.
6. A best-sellers section with a link to each product the visitor can choose.

7. Trust signals and a risk-free message.
8. Benefit copy describing what the product does for the customer.

Tested Superstore theme homepage section order:
1. Utility bar
2. Header
3. Slideshow

4. Highlights banner
5. Featured collections (Collection list)
6. Image with text overlay

7. Featured collection (product grid)
8. Search
9. Highlights banner (repeated near the bottom)

10. Footer
Early-stage high-ticket dropshipping store section list:
1. Announcement bar (fixed).
2. Utility bar (fixed).

3. Header (fixed).
4. Slideshow used as a single static hero image (fixed).
5. Highlights banner.
6. Collection list.

7. Image with text overlay.
8. Featured collection.
9. Footer (fixed). All other default sections such as Grid, Rich Text and Testimonials can be removed.
Conflict between structures: the tested Superstore order has 10 positions and the niche procedure has 4 (plus banner). The early-stage order has 9.
Use the niche structure for a single-product ad landing store and the Superstore order as an example of a full multi-section homepage; the older 2021-2022 orders are examples, not requirements.
Start a new Shopify store's public home page from the basic template, which has an Image with text overlay section and no images or design.
It is changed from the storefront preview using the Edit home page option, as part of the design work after account setup.
Supplier-ready demo store setup (Manhattan theme)
Time: a full homepage customization of a new Shopify theme takes about one hour
when the brand images are already finished.
At the supplier-approval stage the homepage only needs to look credible and work. Advanced mega menu, product card and blog settings can wait until the store is live.

Procedure:
1. Upload all prepared images in one batch under Content > Files > Upload files, select them all and click Open.

2. Go to Online Store > Themes and confirm the Manhattan theme is active.
3. Click Customize and check that the dropdown at the top reads Homepage.
4. Open Theme settings (gear icon) and set logo, favicon, colors, typography, layout, buttons, social media and contact details.
5. Open Header and set sticky header, logo position, menu, menu type, separator line, menu fonts and navigation colors.
6. Edit the Slideshow: keep one slide, add image and text, link the button to a collection.
7. Edit the Collection list: heading, columns, overlay, then add collections and their images.

8. Edit the Featured collection, Image banner (only if needed), Email signup and Pre-footer.
9. Hide Rich text, Blog posts and the Announcement bar until they are needed.
10. Edit the footer and cookie consent, click Save after each section and check the homepage on desktop and on a phone.
Uploading images to Content > Files does not link them to any section. Each image still has to be selected inside its section; the upload only makes them available in the picker.
Imagery and sections should be finished in a supplier-approval demo as credible placeholders; the full store can be refined after launch.
Build order for the initial site (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice)
1. Set up the homepage with the business message and links to the main sections.
2. Set up the collection page template once so every collection uses the same settings.
3. Set up the product page template once so every product uses the same settings.
4. Create all single pages (About Us, Contact Us, policies, terms) and link them into the navigation.
5. Leave the blog untouched until after the business has launched. When steps 1 to 4 are done, the site is ready for the next stage.
Add social media links in the theme settings (the panel where you change your store's look). They sit next to the logo, colors and contact details.
Social media is part of the Supplier-ready demo procedure, a fixed list of steps for preparing a demo store for suppliers, at **step 4**.
Leave social media until **launch** (the day the store goes live for customers). Then add Facebook, Pinterest, email address and Instagram.

The footer (the bottom part of every page) should link to social media pages.
Links to unrelated pages make the store look untrustworthy.
A section is one block on a page, such as a banner or a product list.

Deleting or hiding a section can be undone in the customizer (the visual editor for your theme).
Deleting also removes the section's settings.
For a first version, **hide** sections with the eye icon instead of deleting them.

While building a theme, hide a section you are unsure about with its visibility toggle (an on/off switch).
This lets you restore it without rebuilding. (Shrine theme.)
**Delete** a section only when you are sure you will not need it. (Shrine theme.)

In the first version of a store with **no content yet**, hide Rich text (a formatted text block) and Blog posts (a list of articles).
Enable them later, once content exists.
Hiding vs deleting sections (continued)
To remove a section: click into it. Click the three dots at the top of the panel. Choose **Remove section**.
In a Shopify theme (Shopify is the online store software), the header, announcement bar, utility bar and slideshow sections are fixed. They cannot be removed.
The header is the top of the page. The announcement bar is a thin strip with a message. The utility bar is a small strip with links. The slideshow shows rotating images.

The footer is always part of the site.
Only the optional sections in between can be removed. (Superstore theme, 2021-2022, older advice.)

The Shrine theme editor's Add section panel has a Search sections box.
The search box filters the whole list of section groups.
**Type a section's name** to find it. You do not need to scroll through the groups: Header, Footer, Sections, Others and Apps.

Sections available in the Shrine Pro theme editor, grouped as shown in Customize > Add section:
**Header**: Horizontal Ticker, Announcement bar, Header
**Cart drawer**: Cart drawer
**Home page template**: Slideshow, Comparison table, Icon Bar, Results, Contact Form, Instagram stories, Promo Pop-Up, Scroll to Top Button, Global Music Player
**Footer**: Section divider, Footer
**Sections (main list)**: Featured product, Collection list, Rich text, Image with text, Image banner, Slideshow, Collage, Multicolumn, Multirow, Collapsible content
**Others**: Email signup, Contact form, Video, Blog posts
**Apps**: 3D Parallax hero, Announcement bar, Before & After slider, Bundle deals, Comparison table, Content tabs, Custom Columns V2, Facebook testimonials, Featured on, Horizontal Ticker,
Icons with content, Image/Video Slider, Instagram stories, Music Player, OLD Custom columns, Page scroll progress, Custom Liquid, Page
Checkout branding
The checkout is the page where the customer pays.
Shopify controls the checkout for security. It uses 256-bit encryption, a very strong way of scrambling data.
p.h: Checkout branding: what can be changed

p.t:
Because of this, the checkout cannot be fully redesigned.
Store owners can only add a **custom logo**.
Store owners can add a background image of about **1000 x 400 px** (px means pixels, the small dots that make up a screen).
Store owners can change some colors and buttons.
**Shopify Plus** (a higher, paid Shopify plan) is required to customize the checkout. It costs about **2,500 USD per month**.
Without Shopify Plus, the checkout is the same for all Shopify stores.

Within that limit, upload the brand font (the store's own text style) in Shopify so it appears at checkout.
Set the logo in the checkout settings.
Use a logo with trust signals (small badges that show a customer the store is safe), such as free shipping or a money-back guarantee.
Conflict on access means two sources disagree. One says full checkout customization requires Shopify Plus.

The other describes adding a checkout banner under Settings > Checkout without naming a plan.
**Check your plan** before you promise a custom checkout.

Conflict on size also means two sources disagree. The checkout banner is 1500 × 300 px.
The older source gives a background image of about 1000 × 400 px.
Use **1500 × 300 px** for the checkout banner under Settings > Checkout.
Use the 1000 × 400 px background only where the older Superstore-era guidance applies.
Checkout banner and trust elements
Shopify checkout image: a banner shown at checkout (the checkout banner).

Go to Settings > Checkout and add an image.
Recommended size is **1500 × 300 px**.

Create it in Canva (an online design tool) with custom size 1500 × 300.
Add the logo.
Add trust badges such as Privacy Protected, Secure Checkout and Satisfaction Guaranteed.

Get these badges from Canva's Elements section (its library of ready-made graphics).
